prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of pempek as eaten at a small Palembang eatery in South Sumatra: a plate with a few thick pieces of fried fish-cake — a bright orange-yellow cylinder or torpedo-shaped pempek, golden-brown and crackly on the outside, with a few pieces of the paler variety (pempek lenjer or kapal selam) on the side. A small dish of dark, sweet-sour-tangy cuko sauce (made from palm sugar, vinegar, chili, garlic, and shrimp) into which one piece of pempek has been dipped. A few slices of cucumber and a small portion of yellow mie (vermicelli) on the side. Served on a chipped plain white plate, on a worn wooden or formica warung table, a glass of iced tea and other warung tables softly out of focus behind. Soft natural daylight from the open shopfront, viewed from about 40 degrees above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled serving, slightly messy edges with cuko drips, true-to-life colours, realistic textures. The defining feature is the bright orange-yellow colour of the pempek and the reddish-brown cuko sauce — not golden like tempura, not a generic brown fish cake. No food styling, no microgreens, no lettuce garnish, no Western plates, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
